pr_title: [wasm][debugger] Add resolved assemblies to cache to help mono.cecil find them
pr_body:
When mono.cecil is loading the assembly and this assembly references to another assembly, it searchs for this assembly on a cache and on folders, in our case, we were not adding the assemblies loaded in this cache, so mono.cecil was failing and it was not possible to set breakpoint in any assembly that references another assembly.
Fix #47792

@lewing, I'm not sure who order this assemblies, but yes, if they are in a wrong order will be a problem. I thought that when blazor generates blazor.boot.json it was being ordered there. @captainsafia do you know if the assemblies are ordered before being loaded on blazor?

> Might be useful to log errors from `resolver.ResolveFailure`.

It's logged: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e61c3724b106671e23d61207a8186c9e5c7a962a/src/mono/wasm/debugger/BrowserDebugProxy/DebugStore.cs#L763

> @lewing, I'm not sure who order this assemblies, but yes, if they are in a wrong order will be a problem. I thought that when blazor generates blazor.boot.json it was being ordered there. @captainsafia do you know if the assemblies are ordered before being loaded on blazor?

I think we may be sort of getting lucky because the results of the resolver step insert things in a working order into the json but the runtime doesn't actually require that, it waits for everything to transfer before attempting to load.  I wonder if we should do the same here, it might actually speed up loading because we wouldn't be loading all the other assemblies multiple times.

> The PR description should be more descriptive. It's not clear why the changes are being made. It will also be useful to mention the errors, or issues caused. And does this affect non-dynamically loaded assemblies?

This affect non-dynamically loaded assemblies.

> This affect non-dynamically loaded assemblies.

Does it change the behavior in any case? Can we test what this changes?

The only difference is that now we are able to load assemblies that depends on other assembly, and this is what the test tests, without the implementation the breakpoint does not work.
When Cecil is looking for assembly that is referenced, it doesn't find and could not load the assembly, then the breakpoints don't work.

> @captainsafia do you know if the assemblies are ordered before being loaded on blazor?

I'm a little late here but in case the info is still helpful: we don't do any kind of ordering on the resources listed in the JSON file.

> > @captainsafia do you know if the assemblies are ordered before being loaded on blazor?
> 
> I'm a little late here but in case the info is still helpful: we don't do any kind of ordering on the resources listed in the JSON file.

This certainly won't regress anything and the output of the resolve steps is likely correct but it is probably worth checking if we can improve the situation #49193

issue_context.title: Blazor wasm debugging not working when adding attribute with enum from other project
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug
This was reported in dotnet/aspnetcore#22657 but was thought to be a dupe of dotnet/aspnetcore#22627.  I'm not sure it is.

When using a custom attribute that has an enum from a class library project in it's constructor, Blazor WASM debugging does not work.  The debugger seems to load up fine (`mono_wasm_runtime_ready` in console etc.) but breakpoints are not bound.  (It is not a case of waiting, they never become bound.)

### To Reproduce
1. Create blazor WASM server hosted template
2. Add a class library and reference it from the blazor WASM project
3. Add an enum to the class library
4. In the blazor WASM project add a attribute class that has the above enum in its constructor, and a class that utilises the enum
5. Set a breakpoint in Counter.razor on the increment line
6. Try to debug, and observe how the breakpoint is not bound
7. Comment out the attribute above the class and restart debugging, observe how the breakpoint gets hit

See this repo for reproduction: https://github.com/rathga/BlazorAttribute  Comment the attribute on line 9 of SomeClass.cs to enable the breakpoint.

```csharp
    [Some(SomeEnum.Something)] // <-- comment this to make blazor WASM debugging work
    public class SomeClass  { }
```

### Further technical details
